questions.q: A developer wants fast unit tests for a Kafka Streams topology, without starting a broker. Which tool is meant for that?

options.t: A single-node KRaft cluster started inside each test method
options.why: That works but is slow; TopologyTestDriver needs no broker.

options.t: TopologyTestDriver
MockProducer wired into the StreamsBuilder by hand
options.why: MockProducer tests producer code, not a topology.

options.t: kafka-streams-application-reset run before every test
options.why: The reset tool resets a deployed application's offsets and topics.

questions.explain: `TopologyTestDriver` (in `kafka-streams-test-utils`) pipes records through a `Topology` and simulates the runtime, with no broker.

questions.q: In a `TopologyTestDriver` test, how is a record sent into the topology's input topic?

options.t: With a KafkaProducer pointed at the test driver's port
options.why: The driver has no network port; it has test topic helpers.

options.t: By calling the topology's process() method directly
options.why: The driver feeds records through TestInputTopic.

options.t: pipeInput on a TestInputTopic from createInputTopic
By writing to a file the driver watches for new lines
options.why: The driver doesn't read files.

questions.explain: `createInputTopic(name, keySerializer, valueSerializer)` returns a `TestInputTopic`, whose `pipeInput` sends records (keys, values, timestamps or lists) into the topology.

questions.q: How does a `TopologyTestDriver` test read what the topology wrote to its output topic?

options.t: With readKeyValue on a TestOutputTopic, created with deserializers
With a KafkaConsumer subscribed to the test driver's own in-memory output topic
options.why: There is no broker; the driver captures output itself.

options.t: By querying the driver's changelog topics over HTTP
options.why: The driver offers TestOutputTopic, not HTTP access.

options.t: From System.out, where the driver prints every output record
options.why: Output is captured for TestOutputTopic, not printed.

questions.explain: `createOutputTopic(name, keyDeserializer, valueDeserializer)` returns a `TestOutputTopic`, with helpers such as `readKeyValue` and `isEmpty`.

questions.q: A topology only updates a state store and emits nothing for some inputs. How can a test check that nothing was emitted, and what the store holds?

options.t: Wait 30 seconds, then count all the records stored in the output topic's log
options.why: The driver works synchronously; there's no log to count.

options.t: Assert outputTopic.isEmpty(), then read testDriver.getKeyValueStore(...)
Use interactive queries over the application's RPC layer
options.why: The driver gives direct access to stores; no RPC is needed.

options.t: It can't: stores are private to the topology
options.why: The driver lets tests query its state stores.

questions.explain: The driver captures output records and lets tests query its embedded state stores; `TestOutputTopic.isEmpty()` checks that nothing was emitted.

questions.q: A processor emits a summary on a wall-clock punctuation every 60 seconds. How can a `TopologyTestDriver` test trigger it without waiting?

options.t: Thread.sleep(60_000) in the test
options.why: The driver mocks wall-clock time, so sleeping isn't needed.

options.t: Pipe records with timestamps 60 s apart
options.why: That advances stream time, which drives stream-time punctuations, not wall-clock ones.

options.t: Call the punctuator's punctuate method directly from the test code
options.why: The driver controls punctuation; advancing its clock is the supported way.

options.t: testDriver.advanceWallClockTime(Duration.ofSeconds(60))

questions.explain: The driver mocks wall-clock time: `advanceWallClockTime` triggers wall-clock punctuations. Event-time punctuations fire from piped records' timestamps.

questions.q: A topology uses a stream-time punctuation every 10 seconds. Which `TopologyTestDriver` action triggers it?

options.t: advanceWallClockTime by 10 seconds
options.why: That drives wall-clock punctuations.

options.t: Nothing; punctuations don't run in the test driver
options.why: The driver supports both kinds of punctuation.

options.t: Piping records whose timestamps advance by 10 seconds
Calling testDriver.close(), which flushes punctuations
options.why: close() ends the test; it isn't how punctuations are triggered.

questions.explain: Event-time (stream-time) punctuations are triggered automatically from the timestamps of the records piped in.

questions.q: What should a test do with its `TopologyTestDriver` when it finishes?

options.t: Call testDriver.close()
Delete its internal topics with the Admin API
options.why: The driver has no real topics to delete.

options.t: Nothing; the driver cleans up when garbage-collected
options.why: The docs show closing the driver after each test.

options.t: Run the application reset tool against it
options.why: The reset tool works on deployed applications, not the driver.

questions.explain: The testing guide closes the driver after each test with `testDriver.close()`.

questions.q: Which Maven dependency provides `TopologyTestDriver`, and with which scope?

options.t: kafka-streams, compile scope
options.why: The test driver is in a separate test artifact.

options.t: kafka-clients, test scope
options.why: kafka-clients holds the producer and consumer.

options.t: connect-runtime, provided scope
options.why: That's Kafka Connect.

options.t: kafka-streams-test-utils, test scope

questions.explain: Kafka provides `org.apache.kafka:kafka-streams-test-utils` as a separate artifact, added as a test-scope dependency.

questions.q: Code under test takes a `Producer<String, String>`. Which class lets a unit test check what it sent, with no broker?

options.t: MockProducer, then inspect history()
KafkaProducer with bootstrap.servers=localhost:0
options.why: A real producer needs a broker to send to.

options.t: TopologyTestDriver with a producer topology
options.why: The driver tests Streams topologies.

options.t: MockConsumer reading the producer's output
options.why: MockConsumer can't see a producer's sends.

questions.explain: `MockProducer` is a mock of the producer interface for testing code that uses Kafka; `history()` returns the records sent.

questions.q: A test must check that the application handles a failed send (for example a `TimeoutException`) correctly. How can `MockProducer` simulate it?

options.t: Create it with autoComplete=true, then disconnect the test machine's network
options.why: With autoComplete=true every send succeeds at once.

options.t: Create it with autoComplete=false, then call errorNext(...)
Send a record larger than max.request.size
options.why: MockProducer doesn't enforce broker limits; errorNext is the way to fail a send.

options.t: Call clear() while the send is in progress
options.why: clear() resets the history; it doesn't fail sends.

questions.explain: With `autoComplete=false` sends wait for the test: `completeNext()` succeeds the next one, `errorNext(RuntimeException)` fails it, so error handling can be tested.

questions.q: A `MockProducer` was created with `autoComplete=true`. What happens when the code under test calls `send()` with a callback?

options.t: The send stays pending until completeNext() is called
options.why: That's autoComplete=false.

options.t: The callback runs only after flush()
options.why: With autoComplete=true it completes at once.

options.t: It completes successfully at once and runs the callback
It throws, since a mock can't run callbacks
options.why: Callbacks run on completion.

questions.explain: With `autoComplete=true` each send completes successfully immediately and its callback runs.

questions.q: A test checks how transactional code reacts when another instance takes over its `transactional.id`. Which `MockProducer` method simulates that?

options.t: errorNext(new TimeoutException())
options.why: A timeout is not fencing.

options.t: clear()
options.why: clear() resets the history.

options.t: closed()
options.why: closed() reports whether the producer was closed.

options.t: fenceProducer()

questions.explain: `MockProducer.fenceProducer()` simulates fencing; `transactionCommitted()` and `flushed()` let tests check what the code did.

questions.q: How does a test feed records to code that reads from a `MockConsumer`?

options.t: Assign partitions, set beginning offsets, then addRecord(...)
Send them with a MockProducer that is linked to the consumer under test
options.why: The two mocks aren't linked; records are added to the consumer.

options.t: Write them into a temp file named after the topic
options.why: MockConsumer doesn't read files.

options.t: Pipe them with TestInputTopic.pipeInput
options.why: That belongs to TopologyTestDriver.

questions.explain: Tests assign (or subscribe and `rebalance`) partitions, set offsets with `updateBeginningOffsets`, then `addRecord`; the code's `poll` returns them.

questions.q: Code polls a `MockConsumer` on a background thread. How should a test add records safely?

options.t: Call addRecord from the test thread at any time
options.why: MockConsumer isn't thread safe.

options.t: Wrap every call in a synchronized block on the test class
options.why: The documented approach is schedulePollTask.

options.t: Use a second MockConsumer per thread
options.why: Both threads must use the same consumer under test.

options.t: Use schedulePollTask to run them during the next poll

questions.explain: MockConsumer is not thread safe; `schedulePollTask(Runnable)` lets a test run code during the next `poll` called by a background thread.

questions.q: A test must check that consumer code handles an exception thrown from `poll()`. How can `MockConsumer` do that?

options.t: Add a record with a null value
options.why: A null value is a valid record, not an exception.

options.t: setPollException(...) before the next poll
Call close() and then poll again
options.why: That tests a closed consumer, not the code's handling of a thrown exception.

options.t: Set max.poll.interval.ms to zero
options.why: MockConsumer doesn't run the group protocol.

questions.explain: `setPollException(KafkaException)` makes the next `poll` throw, so tests can exercise error handling (for example of a deserialization failure).

questions.q: Code commits offsets in a `ConsumerRebalanceListener`. How can a `MockConsumer` test exercise a rebalance?

options.t: Start a second MockConsumer in the same group to force a rebalance
options.why: MockConsumer has no group coordinator.

options.t: Change group.id while the test runs
options.why: That doesn't simulate a rebalance.

options.t: Subscribe with the listener, then call rebalance(...)
It can't: rebalances need a real broker
options.why: MockConsumer can simulate them with rebalance().

questions.explain: After subscribing, a test calls `MockConsumer.rebalance(newAssignment)` to simulate partitions being assigned, exercising the rebalance listener.

questions.q: Which TWO tests run without any Kafka broker?

options.t: A Streams topology test with TopologyTestDriver
A load test with kafka-producer-perf-test
options.why: The perf test sends to a real cluster.

options.t: A producer unit test with MockProducer
Reading a topic with kafka-console-consumer
options.why: The console consumer reads from a real cluster.

options.t: Checking lag with kafka-consumer-groups --describe
options.why: This queries a real cluster.

questions.explain: TopologyTestDriver simulates the Streams runtime, and MockProducer/MockConsumer mock the client interfaces, so neither needs a broker; the command-line tools work against a cluster.

questions.q: Before release, a team wants to measure how many records per second a cluster accepts with `acks=all` and 1 KB records. Which tool fits?

options.t: kafka-producer-perf-test
kafka-console-producer with a long input file
options.why: It sends records but doesn't measure throughput or latency.

options.t: kafka-get-offsets run every second
options.why: That reads end offsets; it doesn't load-test.

options.t: MockProducer in a unit test
options.why: A mock has no broker, so it can't measure the cluster.

questions.explain: `kafka-producer-perf-test` (`--num-records`, `--record-size`, `--throughput`, `--command-property`) prints records/sec, MB/sec and latency percentiles.

questions.q: In Kafka 4.3, how do you pass `acks=all` to `kafka-producer-perf-test`?

options.t: --producer-props acks=all, the current option
options.why: --producer-props is deprecated in 4.3.

options.t: --acks all
options.why: There's no dedicated --acks option.

options.t: In an environment variable named KAFKA_ACKS
options.why: The tool takes settings as options.

options.t: --command-property acks=all

questions.explain: The 4.3 perf test takes producer settings with `--command-property k=v`; `--producer-props` is deprecated.

questions.q: Which TWO results does `kafka-producer-perf-test` print?

options.t: Records per second and MB per second
Consumer group lag for each partition
options.why: Lag comes from kafka-consumer-groups.

options.t: Average, maximum and percentile latencies
The broker's CPU usage
options.why: The tool reports client-side figures.

options.t: The number of under-replicated partitions
options.why: That's a broker metric.

questions.explain: The producer perf test prints records/sec, MB/sec, and average, maximum and percentile latencies.

questions.q: After a bug fix, a team wants a test environment's Streams application to reprocess its input from the start. Which TWO steps are needed?

options.t: Run the application reset tool
Delete and recreate the input topics
options.why: The reset tool resets input offsets; the data stays.

options.t: Delete the local state on every instance
Change the brokers' log.retention.hours
options.why: Retention doesn't make an application reprocess.

options.t: Raise num.stream.threads
options.why: Threads don't change where processing starts.

questions.explain: The reset tool resets input offsets and deletes internal topics; local state must be deleted separately on each instance (and output topics handled by downstream consumers).

questions.q: Between two test cases that reuse one `MockProducer`, how is the record history emptied?

options.t: close() and reopen it
options.why: A closed producer isn't reopened.

options.t: flush()
options.why: flush completes pending sends; it doesn't clear history.

options.t: clear()
It can't be emptied; create a new mock
options.why: clear() resets it.

questions.explain: `MockProducer.clear()` resets the history (and other recorded state) for reuse.

questions.q: A unit test fails a `MockProducer` send with a `RecordTooLargeException`. What should well-written application code do?

options.t: Retry the send until it succeeds
options.why: It's non-retriable: the same record will be too large every time.

options.t: Treat it as non-retriable: log or divert the record, not retry it
Raise retries to the maximum integer
options.why: Retries can't fix a record that's too large.

options.t: Ignore it, because the broker retries for you
options.why: Non-retriable errors are reported to the application.

questions.explain: `RecordTooLargeException` is non-retriable (the message will never be sent); testing it with `errorNext` checks that the code handles it rather than retrying.

questions.q: What does `TopologyTestDriver` NOT need, compared with running the application for real?

options.t: Serializers for the input topic
options.why: createInputTopic takes serializers.

options.t: Deserializers for the output topic
options.why: createOutputTopic takes deserializers.

options.t: A Topology to drive
options.why: The driver is built from a Topology.

options.t: A running Kafka cluster

questions.explain: The driver simulates the runtime that fetches records and traverses the topology, so it needs a Topology and serdes, but no broker.
